instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, lemon juice, and 1/2 teaspoon of salt. Mix well to coat the chicken evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Marinated Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until browned on all sides and mostly cooked through, about 6-8 minutes. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt the remaining 3 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the remaining ginger-garlic paste (if any was reserved) and sauté for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Gravy
instructions.text: Add pureed tomatoes, soaked cashews, green cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, bay leaf, and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon of salt. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes are soft and the oil separates.

instructions.title: Blend and Strain the Gravy
instructions.text: Remove the bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and cardamom pods (if easily found). Carefully transfer the gravy mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. For an extra silky texture, pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the clean pan, pressing down on the solids.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the cooked chicken to the smooth gravy. Add crushed kasoori methi and sugar. Stir well and simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to finish cooking thoroughly.

instructions.title: Add Cream and Serve
instructions.text: Stir in the heavy cream. Heat through gently for 1-2 minutes, but do not boil after adding cream as it can curdle. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro before serving with naan or rice.

tips: For the richest flavor, marinate the chicken overnight. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it becomes.
Don't skip blending and straining the gravy; it's key to achieving the signature smooth, restaurant-quality texture of Butter Chicken.
Always add the heavy cream at the very end and gently heat it through without boiling, as boiling can cause the cream to curdle.
article:
Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani: Your Ultimate Indian Lunch Recipe Guide

Few dishes evoke the warmth, comfort, and rich culinary heritage of India quite like Butter Chicken, also known as Murgh Makhani. This iconic dish, celebrated worldwide, is a symphony of flavors and textures, making it a perennial favorite for an Indian lunch. Its creamy, subtly sweet, and tangy tomato-based sauce, enveloping tender pieces of marinated chicken, offers a truly satisfying meal that’s both indulgent and deeply flavorful. If you’ve ever dreamed of recreating this restaurant-quality dish at home, you’re in the right place.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter." Originating in Delhi, India, in the 1950s, it was created by Kundan Lal Jaggi, the founder of Moti Mahal restaurant. The story goes that he developed the dish by combining leftover tandoori chicken with a rich tomato-based gravy made with butter and cream, creating a revolutionary new flavor profile.

This dish is characterized by its vibrant orange-red hue and its incredibly smooth, velvety sauce. The chicken is typically marinated in yogurt and spices before being cooked, traditionally in a tandoor (clay oven), which imparts a smoky flavor. However, it can also be grilled, pan-fried, or baked. The sauce is a luscious blend of pureed tomatoes, ginger, garlic, green chilies, and a medley of aromatic spices like garam masala, fenugreek (kasoori methi), and cardamom, all enriched with copious amounts of butter and cream. The result is a mild yet profoundly flavorful curry that appeals to a wide range of palates, making it a perfect centerpiece for an Indian lunch.

## Ingredients for Butter Chicken

To embark on your Murgh Makhani journey, gather these essential ingredients. Quality matters, especially for the dairy components, to achieve that authentic richness.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 tsp red chili powder (Kashmiri for color, or regular for heat)
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1/2 tsp garam masala
*   1/2 tsp salt
*   1 tbsp lemon juice

For the Makhani Sauce:
*   2 tbsp unsalted butter (and more for finishing)
*   1 tbsp oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1-2 green chilies, slit (optional, adjust to taste)
*   800g canned crushed tomatoes or fresh tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup cashews, soaked in warm water for 15 minutes (for creaminess)
*   1 tsp red chili powder
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1 tsp garam masala
*   1 tsp ground coriander
*   1/2 tsp ground cumin
*   1/2 tsp sugar (or to taste, balances tanginess)
*   1/2 tsp salt (or to taste)
*   1/2 cup heavy cream (plus more for garnish)
*   1 tbsp dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), crushed
*   Water, as needed

## How to Make Butter Chicken: Step-by-Step Guide

Creating this delightful Indian lunch recipe is a rewarding process. Follow these steps for a truly authentic experience.

**Step 1: Marinate the Chicken**
In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring each piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor.

**Step 2: Cook the Chicken**
Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F), or a grill pan/skillet over medium-high heat. If using an oven, arrange chicken on a baking sheet and bake for 15-20 minutes until cooked through and slightly charred. If pan-frying, add a little oil to the pan and cook chicken in batches until golden brown and cooked, about 5-7 minutes per side. Set aside.

**Step 3: Prepare the Sauce Base**
In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt 2 tablespoons of butter with 1 tablespoon of oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and green chilies (if using), and cook for another minute until fragrant.

**Step 4: Build the Flavor**
Add the pureed tomatoes and soaked cashews (drained) to the pot. Stir in red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, ground coriander, and ground cumin. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10-15 minutes, allowing the tomatoes to break down and the spices to meld. The mixture should thicken and the oil should start to separate.

**Step 5: Blend the Sauce**
Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. For an extra silky sauce, you can pass it through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pot.

**Step 6: Finish the Makhani Sauce**
Return the smooth sauce to the pot over low heat. Add the remaining butter, sugar, and salt. Stir until the butter is melted. Stir in the heavy cream and crushed kasoori methi. Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to deepen. Do not boil vigorously after adding cream.

**Step 7: Combine and Serve**
Add the cooked chicken pieces to the sauce. Stir to coat and cook for another 5 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the sauce's flavors and heat through. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

## Pro Tips for the Best Butter Chicken

Achieving that perfect, restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home is within reach with these expert tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it becomes. Overnight is ideal.
*   **Charred Chicken:** If possible, char your chicken slightly. Whether on a grill, under a broiler, or in a very hot pan, a little char adds a smoky depth that is characteristic of authentic Murgh Makhani.
*   **Strain for Silkiness:** After blending the sauce, pushing it through a fine-mesh sieve removes any tiny bits of onion, ginger, or tomato skin, resulting in an incredibly smooth and luxurious gravy. This step truly elevates the texture of your Butter Chicken.
*   **Kasoori Methi:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) are non-negotiable for authentic Murgh Makhani flavor. Crush them between your palms before adding to release their aromatic oils.
*   **Balance of Flavors:** Taste and adjust! The beauty of Butter Chicken lies in its balance of sweet, tangy, and subtly spicy. Add more sugar if too tart, a pinch of chili powder for more heat, or a squeeze of lemon for brightness.
*   **Good Quality Dairy:** Since butter and cream are central to this dish, use the best quality you can find for superior flavor and texture.

## Serving Suggestions for Murgh Makhani

Murgh Makhani is a versatile dish that pairs beautifully with a variety of accompaniments, making it a truly satisfying Indian lunch.

*   **Naan Bread:** The classic pairing! Warm, fluffy naan is perfect for scooping up every drop of that luscious sauce. Garlic naan or butter naan adds an extra layer of flavor.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a lovely contrast to the richness of the curry and helps absorb the flavors.
*   **Roti or Chapati:** For a lighter option, serve with whole wheat roti or chapati.
*   **Salad:** A simple side salad with cucumber, onion, and tomato, dressed with lemon juice, offers a refreshing counterpoint.
*   **Raita:** A cooling yogurt-based raita (cucumber or mint) can balance the richness of the Butter Chicken.

## Variations and Substitutions for Butter Chicken

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is perfect, you can easily adapt it to suit dietary preferences or ingredient availability.

*   **Vegetarian Murgh Makhani:** Replace chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), tofu, or even chickpeas for a delicious vegetarian alternative. Marinate paneer or tofu similarly to the chicken, or pan-fry until golden before adding to the sauce.
*   **Healthier Options:** To reduce fat, use low-fat yogurt for the marinade, skim milk or light cream instead of heavy cream, and reduce the amount of butter. You can also increase the vegetable content in the sauce by adding grated carrots or bell peppers.
*   **Spice Level:** For more heat, add extra green chilies or a pinch of cayenne pepper to the sauce. For a milder version, omit the green chilies entirely and use Kashmiri chili powder, which primarily provides color rather than intense heat.
*   **Chicken Cut:** While boneless thighs are often preferred for their tenderness, chicken breast works well too. Ensure pieces are cut uniformly for even cooking.
*   **Smoked Flavor:** For an authentic smoky touch without a tandoor, you can use the "dhungar" method: place a small heat-proof bowl in the pot with the chicken and sauce, place a burning charcoal in it, drizzle a teaspoon of ghee or oil over the charcoal, and quickly cover the pot for 5-10 minutes.

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is more than just a meal; it's an experience. Its creamy texture, fragrant spices, and tender chicken make it an undeniable star of Indian cuisine and a perfect choice for a hearty, flavorful Indian lunch. Don't be intimidated by the steps; with a little patience, you'll be savoring your homemade masterpiece in no time. Enjoy the rich, comforting flavors of this timeless dish!
